notes: Real footage (user-provided), not synthetic - an 18s clip from a fixed elevated CCTV camera over a 6-lane one-way Chinese urban arterial (Chinese date overlay, '公交专用' bus-lane markings). Vehicle mix is cars/a truck/a bus/one scooter - NOT Karachi's motorcycle-dominant traffic KT-Radar is tuned for. site_config now sets class_source: coco_subset with a matching vehicle_classes list (car/bus/truck/motorcycle/pedestrian/bicycle) and weights: models/yolo26n.pt, a real Ultralytics YOLO26n checkpoint (AGPL-3.0), so this is a normal coco_subset site actually running real detection, not a special case. manual_line_counts and known_speed_checks are still deliberately left empty: nobody has done a careful frame-by-frame line-crossing count or independently verified a speed against this clip. manual_whole_clip_estimate is a DIFFERENT, WEAKER kind of ground truth: the user's own rough estimate from watching the clip once (approximately 10-14 cars, 1 truck, 1 bus, 1-2 motorcycles/scooters over the whole ~18s clip), explicitly sparse sampling with no line-crossing granularity - report.py checks it as a separate range sanity check, never with the same confidence as a real line-crossing MAE, and it never participates in the pass/fail gate. site_config's calibration is still an UNVERIFIED VISUAL ESTIMATE (see its own header comment) - a real run against this clip produced speed_kmh readings roughly in the 9-102 km/h range (mean ~47), plausible order of magnitude but higher than real urban traffic typically runs, consistent with that low-confidence calibration - don't trust these numbers as accurate. The same run also showed nearly every track firing R7_wrong_way with cos_to_legal exactly -1.0, which looks like legal_heading is inverted relative to how this homography maps actual vehicle motion - a config error in this estimated site, not a pipeline bug; left as-is and reported rather than silently corrected, since calibration values are supposed to come from a human measurement, not an agent guess-fixing a guess.
